text:
marta: Heads up — hitting a weird onboarding issue with the Node sampleapp + OTEL logging hook. When I enable @redwood/telemetry the same request_id shows up for multiple concurrent requests in dev. Repro steps below.

marta: Repro (single terminal):
```
git checkout sampleapp-telemetry
npm i @redwood/telemetry@1.4.2
export NODE_ENV=development
export LOG_LEVEL=debug
node server.js
```
marta: Then curl two requests quickly:
```
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/echo?i=1" &
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/echo?i=2" &
```

sam: can you paste the raw logs from the two requests? are you using the Express middleware from the README or the hook-based autopatch?

marta: raw logs (trimmed):
```
{"ts":"2026-03-15T12:01:23.123Z","level":"debug","msg":"incoming","path":"/api/echo","request_id":"rK8a9x"}
{"ts":"2026-03-15T12:01:23.125Z","level":"info","msg":"handler start","path":"/api/echo","request_id":"rK8a9x","i":1}
{"ts":"2026-03-15T12:01:23.126Z","level":"info","msg":"handler start","path":"/api/echo","request_id":"rK8a9x","i":2}
```
marta: i.e. same request_id for i=1 and i=2 concurrently.

alexa: this smells like async context/async_hooks not being re-bound across promises. which Node version? and are you using any worker threads?

marta: Node 18.16.0, no worker threads. It's the dev build (nodemon), so lots of file watchers.

dan: did you try the 1.4.3 patch? We shipped an async-hooks ordering fix for the middleware init last week.

marta: tried 1.4.3 — still repros. I instrumented that the req-id gets assigned in the OTEL hook but only after our redaction middleware runs, so redaction misses PII because it runs before req-id is present.

telemetry-bot: Note: known issue logged as TLM-457 (context rebind + nodemon) — workaround: set REDWOOD_OTEL_HOOK_ORDER=early or initialize telemetry before dev hot-reload.

sam: quick workaround you can try — generate request id at HTTP entry as a guard, then let OTEL overwrite if present. Example Express snippet:
```
app.use((req,res,next)=>{
  if(!req.headers['x-request-id']) req.headers['x-request-id']=`rid-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8)}`
  next()
})
// then telemetry init
require('@redwood/telemetry').init(...)
```

marta: that fixed the duplicate-id symptom locally — thanks. But i still think we should update sampleapp and README to recommend the early guard middleware for dev-mode/hot-reload.

alexa: agreed. also we should add a minimal test that simulates two rapid concurrent requests in CI (super small jest e2e) to catch regression.

dan: I'll open a PR that:
- updates sampleapp to include the guard middleware behind a DEV_MODE flag
- documents REDWOOD_OTEL_HOOK_ORDER
- adds a simple concurrency e2e

marta: awesome — would you also add a note about redaction order? i ran into a case where structured JSON logs had unredacted email field because redaction middleware ran before req-id extraction.

dan: will do. assigning to @alexa for the docs blurb and @sam for the e2e test. @marta can you paste the minimal failing test case into the PR comments?

marta: yep i'll add the logs and a tiny repro script.

sam: quick Q — should we bump the SDK in the sampleapp to 1.5.0 (beta) or keep stable 1.4.x? the 1.5 beta has better init primitives to avoid this ordering problem.

alexa: lean 1.5.0-beta in the branch behind a feature flag, but don't make it default until we smoke test.

marta: sounds good. thanks everyone :pray: 

sam: filing a follow-up task to add a telemetry integration test in the devex backlog. cc @devops

telemetry-bot: TLM-457 updated: add sampleapp guard + docs. PR created: #3421

marta: i'll validate the PR once it's up. thanks all :rocket:
